symbols.name: integer to invert
symbols.meaning: The integer whose inverse modulo M is sought.
symbols.quote: Let $\beta$ be the integer to be inverted and $M \ge 1$ the modulus; the letter $M$ changes meaning here.

symbols.name: modulus
symbols.meaning: A positive integer, the modulus of the inverse.
symbols.quote: Let $\beta$ be the integer to be inverted and $M \ge 1$ the modulus; the letter $M$ changes meaning here.

symbols.name: inverse
symbols.meaning: An integer whose product with beta is congruent to 1 modulo M.
symbols.quote: An inverse is an integer $\mu$ for which $\beta\mu$ is [congruent](congruence-modulo.md) to $1$ modulo $M$, so the inverse is defined by that congruence.

symbols.name: quotient integer
symbols.meaning: The integer with beta mu - 1 = nu M, the quotient (beta mu - 1)/M.
symbols.quote: If $\beta\mu \equiv 1 \pmod M$, then $\beta\mu - 1 = \nu M$ for some integer $\nu$, namely the quotient $(\beta\mu-1)/M$, so every common divisor of $\beta$ and $M$ divides $1$.

symbols.name: axis index
symbols.meaning: The position of an axis among the axes.
symbols.quote: Let $M_i$ be the length of axis $i$, the number of values its coordinate takes, where $i$ is the axis index.

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The number of values the coordinate along axis i takes.
symbols.quote: Let $M_i$ be the length of axis $i$, the number of values its coordinate takes, where $i$ is the axis index.

symbols.name: product of lengths
symbols.meaning: The product of all the axis lengths M_i.
symbols.quote: Put $S = \prod_i M_i$ for their product, and $\pi_i = \prod_{j<i} M_j$ for the product of the lengths before axis $i$, with $\pi_1 = 1$.

symbols.name: prefix product
symbols.meaning: The product of the lengths of the axes before axis i.
symbols.quote: Put $S = \prod_i M_i$ for their product, and $\pi_i = \prod_{j<i} M_j$ for the product of the lengths before axis $i$, with $\pi_1 = 1$.

symbols.name: inverse of prefix product
symbols.meaning: The inverse of pi_i modulo M_i.
symbols.quote: Let $\mu_i$ be the inverse of $\pi_i$ modulo $M_i$, which exists.

symbols.name: generator
symbols.meaning: A generator of a cyclic group of order S, whose powers make up the group.
symbols.quote: Each inverse $\mu_i$ supplies exponents to the paper's map, which acts on $\xi$, a generator of a [cyclic group](cyclic-group.md) of order $S$.

symbols.name: axis generator
symbols.meaning: A generator of a cyclic group of order M_i.
symbols.quote: For each axis $i$, let $\xi_i$ be a generator of a cyclic group of order $M_i$, so $\xi_i^{M_i} = 1$.

symbols.name: positive exponent
symbols.meaning: A positive integer exponent under which the image becomes 1.
symbols.quote: Conversely, let $\kappa$ be a positive integer exponent with $\left(\prod_j \xi_j^{\mu_j}\right)^{\kappa} = 1$, and fix an axis $i$.

relations.quote: An inverse is an integer $\mu$ for which $\beta\mu$ is [congruent](congruence-modulo.md) to $1$ modulo $M$, so the inverse is defined by that congruence.
An inverse of $\beta$ modulo $M$ exists exactly when $\beta$ and $M$ are [coprime](coprime.md), that is, when their greatest common divisor is $1$.

Conversely, the inverse is obtained from [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) applied to $\beta$ and $-M$: it gives integers $\mu$ and $\nu$ with $\beta\mu - \nu M = 1$, so this $\mu$ is an inverse.
Each inverse $\mu_i$ supplies exponents to the paper's map, which acts on $\xi$, a generator of a [cyclic group](cyclic-group.md) of order $S$.
